declared_class.coefficients: prime-independent integer values of fixed bounded-degree polynomials, or more generally coefficient log-height O(log n)
declared_class.exclusions: nonhomogeneous sums, unbounded sparsity/degree, target-dependent coefficients, and the identically zero residual as a height certificate
declared_class.gaps: may move with n, independently of target factorization, with each monomial gap budget O(n/log n)
declared_class.residual_height: H_sum=log(sum_j |c_j| A_j), conservatively before archimedean cancellation

theorem.actual_target_implication: if Q|R then Q/G0 divides R/B and has logarithmic height O(n)
theorem.cancellation_invariant: with B=gcd_j |c_j A_j|, G0=gcd(Q,B), G=gcd(Q,R), X=G/G0, one has X|R/B
theorem.capacity: the sum-only quotient has O(n)=o(n log n) log height; the common product baseline remains the Item282 channel
theorem.deoverlap: all statements hold for every Q|q_n/gcd(q_n,D_m)
theorem.full_qn_identity: a nonzero O(n)-height residual cannot be divisible by q_n for all large n because log q_n=n log n+O(n)
theorem.height: fixed T,K, coefficient log-height O(log n), and monomial gap budget O(n/log n) imply log|R/B|<=O(n)
theorem.homogeneous_reduction: gcd(Q,sum c_j D_j)=gcd(Q,R), R=sum c_j A_j, for every Q|q_n
theorem.unique_minimum: a unique least term valuation gives v_p(R) equal to that minimum; only tied minima contribute to X
theorem.zero_identity: R=0 can force homogeneous scalar divisibility modulo q_n, but supplies no nonzero residual height bound
